title: Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max (256 GB) - Cosmic Orange $1899.00 Delivered @ Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max (256 GB) - Cosmic Orange $1899.00 Delivered @ Amazon AU

[Desijugaad] Same price in Officeworks with all colours..
[Notbigdeal] Beautiful price. Just wandering if iPhone price will increase soon due to chips costs. What do you think
[jay889344] Absolutely will. Not sure why you got negged but iPhone 18 Pro series likely to launch with $200-$300 price bump in Sep
[hawkeye93] Why would they leave iPhone out of the game? Ipad and Macbook already so iPhone next.
[stuarty9] Buy now if you don’t want to pay big $$ for the iPhone 18 Pro
[Franc34] Does Apple store will match the price? then you can use the apple gift cards purchased to pay it for it. Unfortunately the last report is that Apple will increase prices of iphone 18 pro and pro max by USD 200-300 so in AUD price jump might be between AUD$300-500 so iphone 18 pro might start $2,500 and pro max $2,700
[Poison Ivy] JB have gift card deals just as often though so it doesn’t really matter
Apple only matches up to 10% off RRP
[sct911] wow, can see some people that like flagships moving to android with those price rises
[TechVisar] I’m still using my 3.5-year-old iPhone 14 Pro Max. Unfortunately, the charging port is damaged, so I’m relying solely on MagSafe charging.
Do you think the iPhone 18 Pro Max will be a significant upgrade over the 17 Pro Max, or is the difference likely to be minor? I’m trying to decide whether to wait for the 18 Pro Max or buy the 17 Pro Max when it becomes available. Any advice from the followers and experts would be appreciated
[OzBed] iPhones only get incremental updates every year. Just like cars, you need to wait a few years between upgrades to actually feel a difference. For 18 Pro Max, you’re pretty much getting the same phone for a higher price, for obvious reasons
[dottjt] Why not just get the charging port fixed? Even if you were to get the 18 Pro Max, you'd still probably want to fix the 14 Pro Max anyway in order to sell it.
[wfdTamar] I have the same phone (my first iPhone). Dedicated Mac user for 40 years, but I probably wont buy another iPhone. A good android is just as good and cheaper (though it is harder to work out which is good). The Oneplus I had prior was good.
[Mjk698] If you liked OnePlus well the guy who help co-found oneplus also is the founder & developer of NOTHING PHONE, I have owned both Nothing phone 2a and 2 and they are really good devices! Have a Google mate 😁
[MediumRareChicken] I’d go for a 16 Pro Max. I recently bought a 512GB for $850 with brand new genuine battery
[Mjk698] Are you sure? Quick search on Gumtree nothing under $1200…
[MediumRareChicken] FB marketplace https://imgur.com/a/ShtEsF2
[TechVisar] Thank you all for your comments, suggestions, and advice. The general consensus seems to be to get the charging port repaired and keep using my 14 Pro Max for a while longer, rather than upgrading straight away. That’s given me something to seriously consider.
Thanks again to everyone who shared their thoughts and experiences. It’s great to hear different perspectives, and they’ve definitely helped me make a more informed decision.
[OzGuy93] Still on the iphone 13 pro, Really don't see any incentive to upgrade, Feels almost as snappy as the day i bought it. Battery has 88% health. Anyone else feel zero reason to upgrade anytime soon like me?
[SuHao] I have 14 Pro Max and my battery health is at 75%, man it sucks
[StreamHammer] You can get the battery replaced at the Apple Store for around $179. My 14 Pro is currently at 84% and I'm considering getting the battery replaced over the coming months.
[Chickenleg] I just had my 3 and a half year old 14 Pro’s battery replaced recently at 85% - probably could have pushed it out a bit longer. Booked it in and it was ready an hour later ($169). Hoping to squeeze a few more years out of it! Phone technology has definitely hit a stalemate these past few years.
[Mooncakes] @Chickenleg: Did they have to factory reset your phone?
[Chickenleg] @Mooncakes: Nope, I thought they would but it came back same as it was when I dropped it off. They do make sure you’ve backed up your phone though.
[CBrads4] Man I am so frustrated. My 14 Pro Max has a small crack in the back glass. I went to go and get the battery replaced and Apple told me that they can’t do the battery replacement without also replacing the back glass. Fair enough, I understand why that’s the case. Only problem is that the back glass replacement on the 14 Pro Max is $900. It would cost almost $1,000 to replace the battery in the end. Not really worth it. I’ll just carry a power bank if I need to.
[J0hn] same here-iphone 14 pro max with 89% SoH. I’ll keep using until on its last leg
[elitekitty] My iPhone 13 pro is still going, but I am getting a little worried. The camera has a hard time standing up to the current quality of other iPhones. Also battery capacity is now 79%. Might have to bite the bullet soon.
[bugsbunny] How come your battery health is so good? Also on the iPhone 13 Pro, but my battery is 74% lol.
Just upgraded and bought the iPhone 17 Pro. Aside from the battery, USB C is a big incentive for me. Hopefully it’ll last me 5 years like the 13 did.
[Dollar Dreamer] I have this mobile phone and it is good quality. Has good ram size for games and apps and good size storage for photos and videos recorded from camera. The screen also is very sharp. Expensive but this iPhone mobile phone is good quality.
[colin5000] Thanks OP. I’m rocking the 12Pro which was starting to get sluggish (even with a replacement battery 2 years ago) but has improved a lot since installing iOS 27 (public beta). Will hold out for 18Pro and hopefully hold for another six years.
[kaykay4] am also with 12promax i bought 2nd-hand couple of years ago. Maybe will consider 17promax after 18 drops.
[Daabido] It would fly even more if you backed up, reset to factory then restore. It works a treat. Much faster. iOS 27 adds additional speed.
[imaxsameer] When you say restore, do you mean setting it up as avnew device and loading up your data through iCloud, or plugging it into a Mac and doing a restore through there?
